Story: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile
Summary: In his first year, Cyrus of Persia — named in Isaiah's prophecy long before — decreed that the exiles could return to Jerusalem and rebuild God's house, even returning the Temple treasures Nebuchadnezzar had taken. Some 42,000 exiles journeyed home under Sheshbazzar and Zerubbabel.
Significance: God moved the heart of a pagan emperor to fulfil His promise of homecoming, right on Jeremiah's schedule. No exile — of place, habit, or heart — is permanent when God says it is time to come home.
